about.title: Rocklin Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Property owners around Rocklin — from retail centers near Sunset Boulevard to apartment communities off Sierra College Boulevard — have a duty to keep their spaces reasonably safe. When a spill, broken stair, uneven walkway, or poor lighting causes a fall, the property owner isn't automatically responsible; California law asks whether they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That's why what happens right after your fall matters. Photos of the hazard, the names of witnesses, and a written incident report can make the difference in whether a claim holds up. Surveillance footage from stores and complexes is often erased on a set schedule, so time is not on your side. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect Rocklin residents hurt on someone else's property with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain the options, free of charge.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Rocklin Fall

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney knows how to gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Video Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many Rocklin businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. An attorney can send a preservation request quickly so that critical video evidence isn't lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: Because California uses pure comparative fault, a property owner may try to shift blame onto you. An attorney can push back on that narrative and help protect the value of your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Rocklin?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public sidewalk or building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early administrative claim. Because these timelines vary, it's worth talking to an attorney soon rather than waiting.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover even if you share some blame, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. Property owners sometimes argue the injured person wasn't watching where they were walking to reduce their own responsibility. An attorney can help gather evidence that puts the full picture in context.

items.question: I fell at a Rocklin shopping center near Sunset Boulevard — what should I do first?
items.answer: Take photos of the exact spot, including any spill, crack, or debris, before it's cleaned up or repaired. Ask an employee to file an incident report and get the names of anyone who saw what happened. Then consider having an attorney request that the store preserve its surveillance video, since that footage may only be kept a short time.
